entries.title: Cliff diagnosis done: the roads-climb-cliffs bug is WorldForge's street carver, and TileForge is missing nothing
entries.detail: Answers to sl-0028, all measured on the b70 pack, no fixes applied yet. (1) PROVENANCE: high-cliff walkability is WorldForge-side semantics, not TileForge tile properties - terrain.rock sits in the loader's BLOCKED_MATERIALS list, and the cliff terraces are adapter-side ART drawn inside the rock mass under an explicit invariant ('every walkable cell stays level 0 - a cliff can never cross traversal'). The assertion the designer remembers giving is the narrower 2026-07-28 moss ruling: bare moss carpet on LEVEL-0 apron rock walks; terraces stay solid. Measured b70 grid: plateau tops 1705 cells with only 79 walkable (every one a road/lane cell), cliff edges 231 with 29 walkable (lane crossings), apron 781 with 157 walkable (moss + graded trails), and the RAMP layer is ALL ZEROS - ramps are never placed by anything, though the package ships four walkable ramp families. The stated intent (edges unwalkable / tops walkable / ramps the access) is NOT implemented: tops are blocked and ramps do not exist. Making tops walkable is a walkability-CONTRACT change touching pack, game, and world_filler - designer-ruled arc, not a quiet fix. Related: world_filler's 'walkable cliff-top tiles' observation (sl-0026) is actually moss carpets and graded/lane cells, not tops. (2) ROADS x CLIFFS: wilderness trails GRADE rock crossings to gravel (zero violations measured), but the city street-web carvers write lanes with NO rock grading - the b70 snowline city carved 108 walkable lane cells at terrace level >= 1 (x 200-237, y 25-26): streets climbing cliff faces with no ramps. That is the designer's road issue. A second ungraded writer (the landmark approach carver) is latent.
